assessment_summary:
1. Let G be a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph.
Justification: Valid assumption.
2. Since G is bipartite, its vertices partition into two sets U and V where every edge connects U to V.
Justification: Valid, by definition of bipartite.
3. Since G is cubic, every vertex has degree 3, so 3|U| = 3|V|, meaning |U| = |V|.
Justification: Valid, by degree sum formula.
4. Because G is 3-connected, it is also 3-edge-connected and thus bridgeless.
Justification: Valid, vertex connectivity is a lower bound for edge connectivity.
5. By Petersen's theorem, G contains a perfect matching M.
Justification: Valid, every bridgeless cubic graph has a perfect matching.
6. The spanning subgraph G \ M has degree 2 at every vertex.
Justification: Valid, removing a perfect matching from a 3-regular graph leaves a 2-regular graph.
7. The subgraph G \ M is a collection of disjoint cycles covering all vertices of G.
Justification: Valid, 2-regular graphs are collections of disjoint cycles.
8. Since G is bipartite, every cycle in G \ M is an even cycle.
Justification: Valid, bipartite graphs have no odd cycles.
9. Suppose G \ M consists of more than one cycle; then for any cycle C, the edge cut separating C from the rest of the graph has size at least 3 since G is 3-connected.
Justification: Valid, 3-connectivity implies edge connectivity is at least 3.
10. All edges in this cut must belong to M, as the cycles in G \ M are completely contained within their respective vertex sets and no edges of G \ M leave C.
Justification: Valid, by the definition of the cycles in G \ M.
11. Because there are at least 3 matching edges leaving each cycle, we can always choose a pair of these edges to swap with cycle edges to merge all cycles into a single Hamiltonian cycle.
Objection: Invalid, the existence of cross-edges does not guarantee a sequence of valid alternating path swaps that merges all cycles (e.g., the Horton graph is a counterexample).
